Under the SWLS ruling (2026-09-04, 'when a rights holder publishes the same instrument under two different statements of terms, the terms of the page you actually took the wording from govern') an extractor could take the wording from dospert.org or from the 2006 JDM Appendix and ship. Item text is the canonical RAND 36-Item Health Survey 1.0 wording, transcribed verbatim from RAND's own instrument page; the study publishes no item wording and the PLOS S1 workbook's headers are bare codes sf1..sf36 with no variable labels, so there was no data_labels route. data/ojelabi_2019_sf36_sickle_cell.py melts those columns unchanged, so item codes ARE the source column names -- but the source names carry no text, which is why the code derivation grants no exemption here and Step 5b was run. sfN was mapped to SF-36 item N and confirmed two ways: (1) per-item response ranges reproduce the SF-36's block structure exactly (5,5,3x10,2x7,5,6,5,6x9,5,5x4), 0/36 out-of-range items against the shipped option lists, while all 35 cyclic shifts of the mapping produce 2-23 violations; (2) the workbook's own SF-6D 'Health State' 6-digit code is an exact function of the SF-6D input items under this numbering (PF from sf3+sf4+sf12 0/200 misfits, role limitation sf15+sf18 0/200, social functioning sf32 0/200, pain sf21+sf22 0/200, mental health sf24+sf28 7/200, vitality sf27 14/200; best same-arity rivals 20, 36, 117, 17, 33 and 98 misfits). Anchor direction was checked rather than assumed: sf1 correlates -0.16 with the physical-functioning mean and sf2 correlates +0.40 with sf1 and -0.22 with physical functioning, so higher = worse health on both, matching the canonical 1=Excellent / 1=Much better coding. Observations that are NOT defects: sf21 never takes 6 ('Very severe' pain, 0/200) and sf2 never takes 5 ('Much worse'), so the shipped option lists for those two items are one level wider than the sample used; and sf2 is concentrated at 1 ('Much better now than one year ago', 149/200), which is unusual for a sickle-cell sample but is the direction the correlations confirm. sf1 has one stray 'END' text value in the source that the processing script drops. RIGHTS (SF-36 is a named, commercially licensed instrument -- checked before transcribing). Two rights positions exist for the SAME 36 items. RAND developed the 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36) in 1992' and 'All of the surveys from RAND Health Care are public documents, available without charge', publishes the full item wording at rand.org/health-care/surveys_tools/mos/36-item-short-form/survey-instrument.html under terms that reserve NOTHING: 'RAND hereby grants permission to use RAND 36-Item Short Form Health Survey in accordance with the following conditions ... 1. Changes to the Health Survey may be made without the written permission of RAND. However, all such changes shall be clearly identified as having been made by the recipient. 2. [indemnity for translations] 3. [indemnity for use] 4. The user of the 36-Item Health Survey will provide a credit line when printing and distributing this document acknowledging that it was developed at RAND as part of the Medical Outcomes Study. 5. No further written permission is needed for use of this Health Survey.' Conditions 1-5 carry no fee, no permission-required, no non-commercial, no no-derivatives and no no-redistribution term; 1 expressly permits derivatives, 4 is attribution, 5 waives further permission. That is a disclaim-fitness/attribution shape, not a reserved right -- the same clause template already ruled SHIP for the RAND NEI VFQ-25 in batch_117 (instrument_rights_register.csv). (b) Optum/QualityMetric license the SF-36v2 for a fee and hold the SF-36 trademark. Ojelabi et al. state they administered 'The Short Form (SF-36) version 1 health survey [Ware & Sherbourne 1992]', i.e. the version RAND publishes free, not the fee-licensed v2; and the wording shipped here was copied from RAND's page, not from any Optum document. Under the source-page rule (ECR-R 2026-09-04, SWLS 2026-09-04: the terms of the page the wording was actually taken from govern) this ships.
